body:
# Problem

When a diagnostic is set on an **unloaded** buffer with a `lnum` that is beyond the
end of the file (e.g. LSP sending `publishDiagnostics` for a file that was added with
`bufadd()` but not yet read from disk, where the diagnostic carries a line number from
stale/unsaved content), loading the buffer later crashes the underline handler.

The underline handler calls

```lua
api.nvim_buf_get_lines(diagnostic.bufnr, diagnostic.lnum, diagnostic.lnum + 1, true)
```

with `strict_indexing = true` but never clamps `diagnostic.lnum` to the buffer's line
count. If `diagnostic.lnum >= line_count`, the call throws `E565: Index out of bounds`.

This is the same class of bug fixed for the **signs** handler in #29321
(`fix(diagnostics): don't apply extmarks to invalid lines`) — but the underline handler
was missed. The location-extmark setup in `vim.diagnostic.set` also clamps with
`math.min(diagnostic.lnum, last_row)`.

# Steps to reproduce

```lua
-- minimal standalone reproduction (nvim --headless -u NONE)
local fname = "/tmp/repro.txt"
io.open(fname, "w"):write("line1\nline2\nline3\n"):close()

local ns = vim.api.nvim_create_namespace("repro")
local b = vim.fn.bufadd(fname)          -- unloaded buffer
vim.bo[b].buflisted = true

-- set a stale diagnostic whose lnum is beyond the 3-line file
vim.diagnostic.set(ns, b, {
  { lnum = 100, col = 0, end_lnum = 100, end_col = 1,
    severity = vim.diagnostic.severity.ERROR, message = "stale", bufnr = b },
})

vim.cmd("buffer " .. b)   -- loads file from disk -> BufRead -> deferred underline handler
```

# Expected behavior

No error. The out-of-range diagnostic is simply skipped (its underline is not drawn),
just like the signs handler does.

# Actual behavior

```
Error executing vim.schedule lua callback: .../nvim/runtime/lua/vim/diagnostic.lua:1845:
Index out of bounds
stack traceback:
        [C]: in function 'nvim_buf_get_lines'
        .../nvim/runtime/lua/vim/diagnostic.lua:1845: in function 'fn'
        .../nvim/runtime/lua/vim/diagnostic.lua:1747: in function 'fn'
        .../nvim/runtime/lua/vim/diagnostic.lua:1356: in function <.../vim/diagnostic.lua:1355>
        [C]: in function 'nvim_exec2'
        [string "vim/_core/editor"]:355: in function 'cmd'
```

This is triggered in practice by file pickers (e.g. snacks.nvim) that create buffers
with `bufadd(path)` and then open them with `:buffer`, while an LSP server has already
emitted diagnostics for that URI.

# Root cause

`vim/diagnostic.lua` (0.12.x) / `vim/diagnostic/_handlers.lua` (master), in
`M.handlers.underline.show`:

```lua
for _, diagnostic0 in ipairs(diagnostics) do
  local higroups = { underline_highlight_map[diagnostic0.severity] }
  ...
  local lines =
    api.nvim_buf_get_lines(diagnostic0.bufnr, diagnostic0.lnum, diagnostic0.lnum + 1, true)
  -- ^^^ strict_indexing = true -> throws when diagnostic0.lnum >= line_count
end
```

The `diagnostics` are captured by `show_once_loaded` -> `once_buf_loaded`, which defers
the actual drawing until the buffer is loaded (a `BufRead` autocmd). By the time the
buffer is loaded from disk, its content can be shorter than the `lnum` the diagnostic
carried, so the range is now invalid.

# Suggested fix

Add the same guard the signs handler already has (#29321): compute `line_count` once and
skip diagnostics whose `lnum` is out of range.

```lua
local line_count = api.nvim_buf_line_count(bufnr)
for _, diagnostic0 in ipairs(diagnostics) do
  if diagnostic0.lnum < line_count then
    -- ... existing underline drawing logic ...
  end
end
```

# Environment

- Neovim version: v0.12.4 (also confirmed present on `master`)
- OS: macOS (darwin), aarch64

# Related

- #29321 `fix(diagnostics): don't apply extmarks to invalid lines` (signs handler guard)
- #34085 `fix(diagnostics): diagnostic just after EOL is not drawn`
- #16349 (diagnostics past end of line)
title: vim.diagnostic.handlers.underline.show throws "Index out of bounds" (E565) for stale diagnostics with lnum past end of buffer
